# About the Property

The Pecos Trail Inn is a comfortable, clean, and friendly motor lodge that is close to the historic Santa Fe Plaza and all the adventures Northern New Mexico has to offer.

### **What you’ll find at our Santa Fe motor lodge**

Our rooms are spacious, clean and thoughtfully decorated. Every room is unique in some way. Some of our rooms have themes. You’ll have some room to spread out and store your gear. The beds are comfortably luxurious. The views from the rooms are great and Santa Fe sunsets are some of the best there are.

The Pecos Trail Inn is located conveniently just off the highway, close to hiking and biking trails and only a couple miles from downtown. We’re in a quiet neighborhood, away from the hustle and bustle of the Cerrillos Rd. hotels and motels.

### **All the things!**

*   The best pool in town – open seasonally
*   Bike repair station
*   In-room bike/gear storage in some rooms
*   2.7 miles to the historic Santa Fe Plaza
*   15 miles to Ski Santa Fe
*   20 min bike ride to downtown
*   Hiking and biking trails close to the motel
*   Dog friendly
*   WiFi
*   Event space

### **Coming soon!**

*   Outdoor community space
*   In-room bike/gear storage in more rooms
*   Guest room updates and property renovations

![Image 2](https://thepecostrailinn.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/old-photo-800x785.webp)

### **History of The Pecos Trail Inn**

The Pecos Trail Inn originally opened in 1955 as the Town House Inn, when the southeast side of Santa Fe was just pinon trees and gravel roads. It was the heyday of the road trip, when the post-war economy was booming and American workers had disposable income (and time) to pack up the family and hit the open road.

The Town House was a destination, not just for travelers, but for locals, too. The old lounge(now our event space) was a swanky place with a dance floor and surf and turf for everyone. The pool was surrounded by glass walls and shuffleboard was played in the shade. The property was nice enough to welcome movies stars of the day, including John Wayne. Santa Fe has always been a destination for Western movie productions, with several Western movie sets outside of town.

In the late 60’s the Ellis family bought the Town House, packed up from Ohio and moved into what is now the small 2-bedroom managers suite of the motel. At some point they renamed it Pecos Trail Inn and expanded the property to include what is now the restaurant and the casitas on property.

The Ellis family ran and cared for the motel until we purchased it! While the property does need some renovations to fit our vision of a retro-modern, family-friendly motor lodge, you can rest assured that this place is super clean, really comfortable, and in great working order. We continue to update rooms and our exterior spaces in what will be a multi-year project.

# About the Owners

![Image 2](https://thepecostrailinn.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/snowboarding-640x800.webp)![Image 3](https://thepecostrailinn.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/feet-600x800.jpg)![Image 4](https://thepecostrailinn.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/usatbbq-600x800.jpg)

Sometimes, the universe really does speak to you. It’s a very Santa Fe way of thinking, but even the skeptical people hear it sometimes.

We’re Leah and Adam Vincent and we’re embarking on this crazy little adventure together. In 2013 we moved back to Santa Fe after a few years away. The city had a hold on us — it’s where we met and were married, after all — and we had to come back.

We happen to live in the neighborhood behind The Pecos Trail Inn. Leah, who’s education and background is in hospitality, would say on our walks “How cool would it be to own this place?” This theme would come up again and again.

In 2020 we saw it was up for sale. Around the same time Leah was laid off because of COVID-19 and, with Adam’s encouragement, all of her energy and focus went into making their dreams come true. People thought we were crazy to want to run a hospitality property during a pandemic and banks weren’t keen on the idea at all.

But the universe kept giving us green lights. Behind the scenes the then-owners were rooting for us and being very helpful. Our friends and acquaintances have been incredibly generous to us. Here we are today, thrilled about the future and the journey that will come with it. It’s been a long time in the works, but we can’t wait to welcome you into what now feels like home!

Now that it has been a couple years since we took over this lovely property, it is incredibly rewarding to have the neighborhood embrace us the way and to hear travelers’ stories of staying at Pecos Trail Inn for decades. We have found an even deeper affection for the property as learn how much Pecos Trail Inn means to our community and to the people that grew up in Santa Fe. There is a rich history here and we’re so happy to be writing the next chapter.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 4: Wikimedia Commons logo](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/4a/Commons-logo.svg/40px-Commons-logo.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Commons-logo.svg)

Wikimedia Commons has media related to [Museums in New Mexico](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Museums%20in%20New%20Mexico "commons:Category:Museums in New Mexico").

This **list of museums in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico")** is a list of [museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum "Museum"), defined for this context as institutions (including [nonprofit organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization"), government entities, and private [businesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business "Business")) that collect and care for objects of cultural, artistic, scientific, or historical interest and make their collections or related exhibits available for public viewing. Museums that exist only in cyberspace (i.e., [virtual museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_museum "Virtual museum")) are not included.

_To use the sortable table, click on the icons at the top of each column to sort that column in alphabetical order; click again for reverse alphabetical order._

Wikimedia Commons has media related to [Museums in New Mexico](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Museums%20in%20New%20Mexico "commons:Category:Museums in New Mexico").

This **list of museums in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico")** is a list of [museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum "Museum"), defined for this context as institutions (including [nonprofit organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization"), government entities, and private [businesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business "Business")) that collect and care for objects of cultural, artistic, scientific, or historical interest and make their collections or related exhibits available for public viewing. Museums that exist only in cyberspace (i.e., [virtual museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_museum "Virtual museum")) are not included.

_To use the sortable table, click on the icons at the top of each column to sort that column in alphabetical order; click again for reverse alphabetical order._

The **New Mexico History Museum** is a [history museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum#Historic_houses "Museum") in [Santa Fe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico"), [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), US. It is part of the state-run [Museum of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_New_Mexico "Museum of New Mexico") system operated by the [New Mexico Department of Cultural Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Department_of_Cultural_Affairs "New Mexico Department of Cultural Affairs").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-1) Opened in 2009, the museum houses 96,000 square feet (8,900 m 2) of permanent and rotating exhibits covering the history of New Mexico from ancient Native American cultures to the present.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-2)

The museum was built after the Museum of New Mexico's collection of historic artifacts had outgrown its previous home at the 400-year-old [Palace of the Governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_the_Governors "Palace of the Governors").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-3) The new [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US$ "US$")44 million museum opened to the public on May 24, 2009, holdings around 20,000 artifacts,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-4) and receiving more than 10,000 visitors on its first day.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-5)

The New Mexico History Museum.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-webpage-6) has 3½ floors of exhibitions telling the stories that made the American West, from the early lives of Native people to Spanish colonists. The museum has a section for the Fray Angélico Chávez History Library and Photo Archives.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-webpage-6) It also has the Palace Print Shop & Bindery, and the Native American Artisans Program. 501 New Mexicans were killed in the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World_War "First World War").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-abatemarco-7) On 11 November 2018, the 100th anniversary of [the Armistice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armistice_of_11_November_1918 "Armistice of 11 November 1918"), New Mexico History Museum opened "The First World War" exhibit.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-abatemarco-7)

## Facilities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_History_Museum&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Facilities")]

In addition to the main building, the museum campus includes the following facilities:

*   [Palace of the Governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_the_Governors "Palace of the Governors")
*   Fray Angélico Chávez History Library
*   Palace Press
*   Photo Archives

The **New Mexico History Museum** is a [history museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum#Historic_houses "Museum") in [Santa Fe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico"), [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), US. It is part of the state-run [Museum of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_New_Mexico "Museum of New Mexico") system operated by the [New Mexico Department of Cultural Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Department_of_Cultural_Affairs "New Mexico Department of Cultural Affairs").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-1) Opened in 2009, the museum houses 96,000 square feet (8,900 m 2) of permanent and rotating exhibits covering the history of New Mexico from ancient Native American cultures to the present.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-2)

The museum was built after the Museum of New Mexico's collection of historic artifacts had outgrown its previous home at the 400-year-old [Palace of the Governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_the_Governors "Palace of the Governors").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-3) The new [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US$ "US$")44 million museum opened to the public on May 24, 2009, holdings around 20,000 artifacts,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-4) and receiving more than 10,000 visitors on its first day.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-5)

The New Mexico History Museum.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-webpage-6) has 3½ floors of exhibitions telling the stories that made the American West, from the early lives of Native people to Spanish colonists. The museum has a section for the Fray Angélico Chávez History Library and Photo Archives.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-webpage-6) It also has the Palace Print Shop & Bindery, and the Native American Artisans Program. 501 New Mexicans were killed in the [First World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_World_War "First World War").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-abatemarco-7) On 11 November 2018, the 100th anniversary of [the Armistice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armistice_of_11_November_1918 "Armistice of 11 November 1918"), New Mexico History Museum opened "The First World War" exhibit.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_History_Museum#cite_note-abatemarco-7)

*   Fray Angélico Chávez History Library
*   Palace Press
*   Photo Archives

The **New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science** is a [natural history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_history "Natural history") and [science museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_museum "Science museum") in [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico") near [Old Town Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque"). The Museum was founded in 1986.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-1) It operates as a public revenue facility of the New Mexico Department of Cultural Affairs.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The museum was created by an act of the [New Mexico Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Legislature "New Mexico Legislature") signed into law by Governor [Bruce King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_King "Bruce King") in March 1980.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-2) Part of the motivation for the project was to provide a home for some of the numerous dinosaur fossils discovered in New Mexico rather than sending them to out-of-state institutions.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-3) Ground was broken on a 4.8-acre (1.9 ha) site near [Old Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque") and the museum opened on January 11, 1986. It was one of the first new natural history museums in the U.S. in decades and represented an updated approach focusing on interactive multimedia exhibits rather than large collections of specimens displayed in glass cases.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-4) An astronomy center including an observatory and planetarium was added to the museum in 1999. This was originally a separate museum operated by the [University of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_New_Mexico "University of New Mexico"), but was merged into the Museum of Natural History and Science in 2007.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-6)

## Permanent exhibits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Permanent exhibits")]

Time Tracks, the Museum's permanent exhibit halls illustrate a journey through time, covering the birth of the Universe (≈13.6 billion years ago) to the [Ice Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleistocene "Pleistocene") (≈10,000 years ago). The eight journey through time halls are as follows:

*   Bradbury Stamm Construction Hall of Ancient Life
*   Dawn of the Dinosaurs
*   Jurassic Age of Super Giants
*   New Mexico's Seacoast
*   Age of Volcanoes
*   Rise of the Recent - Evolving Grasslands
*   Cave Experience
*   New Mexico's Ice Age

Other permanent exhibits include an interactive [planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium "Planetarium") where programs are held daily.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) There is also a floor of exhibit galleries dedicated to astronomy and space exploration, as well as an observation deck for viewing through the telescope. The observatory opens only occasionally, usually during evenings when the museum itself is open to the public. The Fossilworks exhibit shows people removing material from fossilized dinosaur bones.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) The museum houses a "Naturalist Center" that is home to live animals and insects, and there is also a geologic exhibit on the minerals of the region.

## Temporary exhibits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Temporary exhibits")]

**Current Exhibits**_Back to Bones_ features "everything from 300-million-year-old fish and early reptiles, dinosaur skulls from near the end of the Age of Reptiles, to Ice Age mammals," according to Paleontology Curator Thomas A. Williamson. The exhibit was originally conceived to showcase New Mexican fossils not only to the public, but also to visiting members of the [Society of Vertebrate Paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Vertebrate_Paleontology "Society of Vertebrate Paleontology") during Albuquerque's hosting of the SVP meeting in October 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-8) The exhibit was renewed in October 2019 and was still on display as of January 2021.

**Previous Exhibits** Until early 2017, the New Mexico Museum of Natural History was home to _STARTUP: Albuquerque and the Personal Computer Revolution_. This exhibit was dedicated to the history of the [personal computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computer "Personal computer") and operated for ten years, being based on a concept by Microsoft co-founder [Paul G. Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen "Paul Allen"), who along with [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates") started [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") in Albuquerque. In May 2007, two exhibits in the _STARTUP_ Gallery won MUSE awards from the [American Alliance of Museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Alliance_of_Museums "American Alliance of Museums"): _Pizza Run - A Slice of Programming_ won a Silver Level MUSE Award in the category of Interactive Kiosks, and the artifact theater _Rise of the Machines_ won a Gold Level MUSE Award in the Multimedia Installations Category. In 2017, the museum relinquished control of this exhibit to Paul Allen to use at his Living Computer Museum + Labs in Seattle, WA.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-9)

The museum previously hosted an exhibit entitled _Wild Music_ from June 2017 through January 2018. The exhibit showcased an interactive collection of both natural and artificial musical displays on the second floor, all with fully bilingual signage. Acoustical physics and musical theory are presented in various ways and from various parts of the world.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-10)

In February 2018 through August of the same year, the museum brought in _Da Vinci: The Genius_ to display recreations of the art and scientific inventions of Leonardo da Vinci. Produced by Grande Exhibitions, the replicas of da Vinci's art and machines focused on the extraordinary achievements of one of the renaissance's most famous and influential people.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-11) Composed of two distinct sections, _Da Vinci: The Genius_ firstly looked deeply into his art, taking a forensic approach to dissecting the Mona Lisa with "The Secrets of Mona Lisa". Secondly, "The Inventions" portion showed 75 separate devices, both small scale and life-sized, invented by Leonardo da Vinci.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-12)

_Picturing the Past_ was a juried exhibition of paleo-art. The gallery featured art from artists worldwide, focusing on prehistoric creatures. The work of local paleoartist [Matt Celeskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Celeskey?action=edit&redlink=1 "Matt Celeskey (page does not exist)") featured heavily. This exhibit was on display through January 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-13)

_Drugs: Costs and Consequences_ was an exhibit that discussed illicit drugs. The exhibit was on display until December 8, 2019.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-14)

_Brain: The Inside Story_ was a traveling exhibition on loan from the American Museum of Natural History. It used hands-on displays to explore senses, emotions, and brain development. Using current research and technology, the exhibit focused on the latest in neuroscience to highlight the brain's amazing abilities in function and adaptation. This exhibit was at the museum until November 10, 2019, after which it was permanently retired, and did not go on to be displayed elsewhere.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-15)

**Upcoming Exhibits** No upcoming exhibits are currently available.

### Dinosaurs exhibited

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Dinosaurs exhibited")]

The _Jurassic Super Giants_ exhibit features the complete skeletons of _[Seismosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seismosaurus "Seismosaurus")_, _[Saurophaganax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saurophaganax "Saurophaganax")_, _[Stegosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stegosaurus "Stegosaurus")_, and one leg of a _[Brachiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachiosaurus "Brachiosaurus")_. Previously, in the museum's atrium was the skeleton of [Stan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Specimens_of_Tyrannosaurus#%22Stan%22:_BHI_3033 "Specimens of Tyrannosaurus"), a _[Tyrannosaurus rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus "Tyrannosaurus")_ measuring forty feet (≈12.2 meters) in length and twelve feet (≈3.7 meters) in height, the second largest _T. rex_ ever found. Stan currently resides at the Farmington Museum in Farmington, NM. Stan was replaced in the atrium during the summer of 2019 by an animatronic Bisti Beast, or _[Bistahieversor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistahieversor "Bistahieversor")_, dinosaur.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-16)

Bronze statues of two dinosaurs created by artist David A. Thomas, a _[Pentaceratops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentaceratops "Pentaceratops")_ named "Spike" and an _[Albertosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertosaurus "Albertosaurus")_ named "Alberta", stand at the entrance.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) Spike and Alberta were installed at the museum in the mid-1980s, with Spike being put in place in 1985[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-17) and Alberta joining a few years later in 1987.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-18) Many dinosaur [fossils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossils "Fossils") have been found in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), and a few of the ones on display in the museum are only known from New Mexico.

## Other features

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other features")]

The Museum also houses changing exhibits, NatureWorks Discovery Store, as well as the Dynatheater, which is a 3-D [theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movie_theater "Movie theater") similar to [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX"). The films shown are typically documentary style, focusing on a broad range of subjects. The exterior of the museum features "A Walk Through New Mexico," a landscape representation of the topographical and geologic features of New Mexico.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

The **New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science** is a [natural history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_history "Natural history") and [science museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_museum "Science museum") in [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico") near [Old Town Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque"). The Museum was founded in 1986.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-1) It operates as a public revenue facility of the New Mexico Department of Cultural Affairs.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The museum was created by an act of the [New Mexico Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Legislature "New Mexico Legislature") signed into law by Governor [Bruce King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_King "Bruce King") in March 1980.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-2) Part of the motivation for the project was to provide a home for some of the numerous dinosaur fossils discovered in New Mexico rather than sending them to out-of-state institutions.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-3) Ground was broken on a 4.8-acre (1.9 ha) site near [Old Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque") and the museum opened on January 11, 1986. It was one of the first new natural history museums in the U.S. in decades and represented an updated approach focusing on interactive multimedia exhibits rather than large collections of specimens displayed in glass cases.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-4) An astronomy center including an observatory and planetarium was added to the museum in 1999. This was originally a separate museum operated by the [University of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_New_Mexico "University of New Mexico"), but was merged into the Museum of Natural History and Science in 2007.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-6)

## Permanent exhibits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Permanent exhibits")]

Time Tracks, the Museum's permanent exhibit halls illustrate a journey through time, covering the birth of the Universe (≈13.6 billion years ago) to the [Ice Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleistocene "Pleistocene") (≈10,000 years ago). The eight journey through time halls are as follows:

*   Bradbury Stamm Construction Hall of Ancient Life
*   Dawn of the Dinosaurs
*   Jurassic Age of Super Giants
*   New Mexico's Seacoast
*   Age of Volcanoes
*   Rise of the Recent - Evolving Grasslands
*   Cave Experience
*   New Mexico's Ice Age

Other permanent exhibits include an interactive [planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium "Planetarium") where programs are held daily.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) There is also a floor of exhibit galleries dedicated to astronomy and space exploration, as well as an observation deck for viewing through the telescope. The observatory opens only occasionally, usually during evenings when the museum itself is open to the public. The Fossilworks exhibit shows people removing material from fossilized dinosaur bones.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) The museum houses a "Naturalist Center" that is home to live animals and insects, and there is also a geologic exhibit on the minerals of the region.

## Temporary exhibits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Temporary exhibits")]

**Current Exhibits**_Back to Bones_ features "everything from 300-million-year-old fish and early reptiles, dinosaur skulls from near the end of the Age of Reptiles, to Ice Age mammals," according to Paleontology Curator Thomas A. Williamson. The exhibit was originally conceived to showcase New Mexican fossils not only to the public, but also to visiting members of the [Society of Vertebrate Paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Vertebrate_Paleontology "Society of Vertebrate Paleontology") during Albuquerque's hosting of the SVP meeting in October 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-8) The exhibit was renewed in October 2019 and was still on display as of January 2021.

**Previous Exhibits** Until early 2017, the New Mexico Museum of Natural History was home to _STARTUP: Albuquerque and the Personal Computer Revolution_. This exhibit was dedicated to the history of the [personal computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computer "Personal computer") and operated for ten years, being based on a concept by Microsoft co-founder [Paul G. Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen "Paul Allen"), who along with [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates") started [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") in Albuquerque. In May 2007, two exhibits in the _STARTUP_ Gallery won MUSE awards from the [American Alliance of Museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Alliance_of_Museums "American Alliance of Museums"): _Pizza Run - A Slice of Programming_ won a Silver Level MUSE Award in the category of Interactive Kiosks, and the artifact theater _Rise of the Machines_ won a Gold Level MUSE Award in the Multimedia Installations Category. In 2017, the museum relinquished control of this exhibit to Paul Allen to use at his Living Computer Museum + Labs in Seattle, WA.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-9)

The museum previously hosted an exhibit entitled _Wild Music_ from June 2017 through January 2018. The exhibit showcased an interactive collection of both natural and artificial musical displays on the second floor, all with fully bilingual signage. Acoustical physics and musical theory are presented in various ways and from various parts of the world.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-10)

In February 2018 through August of the same year, the museum brought in _Da Vinci: The Genius_ to display recreations of the art and scientific inventions of Leonardo da Vinci. Produced by Grande Exhibitions, the replicas of da Vinci's art and machines focused on the extraordinary achievements of one of the renaissance's most famous and influential people.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-11) Composed of two distinct sections, _Da Vinci: The Genius_ firstly looked deeply into his art, taking a forensic approach to dissecting the Mona Lisa with "The Secrets of Mona Lisa". Secondly, "The Inventions" portion showed 75 separate devices, both small scale and life-sized, invented by Leonardo da Vinci.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-12)

_Picturing the Past_ was a juried exhibition of paleo-art. The gallery featured art from artists worldwide, focusing on prehistoric creatures. The work of local paleoartist [Matt Celeskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Celeskey?action=edit&redlink=1 "Matt Celeskey (page does not exist)") featured heavily. This exhibit was on display through January 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-13)

_Drugs: Costs and Consequences_ was an exhibit that discussed illicit drugs. The exhibit was on display until December 8, 2019.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-14)

_Brain: The Inside Story_ was a traveling exhibition on loan from the American Museum of Natural History. It used hands-on displays to explore senses, emotions, and brain development. Using current research and technology, the exhibit focused on the latest in neuroscience to highlight the brain's amazing abilities in function and adaptation. This exhibit was at the museum until November 10, 2019, after which it was permanently retired, and did not go on to be displayed elsewhere.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-15)

**Upcoming Exhibits** No upcoming exhibits are currently available.

### Dinosaurs exhibited

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Dinosaurs exhibited")]

The _Jurassic Super Giants_ exhibit features the complete skeletons of _[Seismosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seismosaurus "Seismosaurus")_, _[Saurophaganax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saurophaganax "Saurophaganax")_, _[Stegosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stegosaurus "Stegosaurus")_, and one leg of a _[Brachiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachiosaurus "Brachiosaurus")_. Previously, in the museum's atrium was the skeleton of [Stan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Specimens_of_Tyrannosaurus#%22Stan%22:_BHI_3033 "Specimens of Tyrannosaurus"), a _[Tyrannosaurus rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus "Tyrannosaurus")_ measuring forty feet (≈12.2 meters) in length and twelve feet (≈3.7 meters) in height, the second largest _T. rex_ ever found. Stan currently resides at the Farmington Museum in Farmington, NM. Stan was replaced in the atrium during the summer of 2019 by an animatronic Bisti Beast, or _[Bistahieversor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistahieversor "Bistahieversor")_, dinosaur.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-16)

Bronze statues of two dinosaurs created by artist David A. Thomas, a _[Pentaceratops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentaceratops "Pentaceratops")_ named "Spike" and an _[Albertosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertosaurus "Albertosaurus")_ named "Alberta", stand at the entrance.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) Spike and Alberta were installed at the museum in the mid-1980s, with Spike being put in place in 1985[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-17) and Alberta joining a few years later in 1987.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-18) Many dinosaur [fossils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossils "Fossils") have been found in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), and a few of the ones on display in the museum are only known from New Mexico.

## Other features

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other features")]

The Museum also houses changing exhibits, NatureWorks Discovery Store, as well as the Dynatheater, which is a 3-D [theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movie_theater "Movie theater") similar to [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX"). The films shown are typically documentary style, focusing on a broad range of subjects. The exterior of the museum features "A Walk Through New Mexico," a landscape representation of the topographical and geologic features of New Mexico.

Right here on property!

# "a true hidden gem"

### **New Mexican CUISINE**X **For Chile lovers**

## "The trail to something special"

By Tantri Wija

For The Santa Fe New Mexican

> The Pecos Trail Café is a true hidden gem — you may have never even heard of it, or even driven by it. The name lets you know where it is (2239 Old Pecos Trail). It’s near nothing except the Old Pecos Trail Inn next door, with which the café has a symbiotic relationship. But Antuna has quietly owned the Pecos Trail Café for five years, catering to a loyal cadre of regulars and guests of the inn, serving some of Santa Fe’s best New Mexican food to those lucky enough to have discovered the place.
> 
> 
> As the Pecos Trail Café, it is a warm, unassuming place with a vaguely cowboy kitsch, family-friendly vibe. Everything is prepared fresh in the kitchen, including its own flour tortillas.
> 
> 
> Jorge Antuna and Jesus Rivera are both from Durango, Mexico. They have been in the food industry for over 20 years. These years of experience were needed to make your dining experience the best it can be.
> 
> 
> **_“You can come and enjoy your family and relax. That’s the main idea of what we’re doing … people are guests the first time, and then they become family.” - Jorge Antuna_**
> 
> 
> **_“It is important for us to give you a New Mexican cuisine experience with a hint of Mexican culture.” - Jesus Rivera_**

## "The trail to something special"

By Tantri Wija

For The Santa Fe New Mexican

> The Pecos Trail Café is a true hidden gem — you may have never even heard of it, or even driven by it. The name lets you know where it is (2239 Old Pecos Trail). It’s near nothing except the Old Pecos Trail Inn next door, with which the café has a symbiotic relationship. But Antuna has quietly owned the Pecos Trail Café for five years, catering to a loyal cadre of regulars and guests of the inn, serving some of Santa Fe’s best New Mexican food to those lucky enough to have discovered the place.
> 
> 
> As the Pecos Trail Café, it is a warm, unassuming place with a vaguely cowboy kitsch, family-friendly vibe. Everything is prepared fresh in the kitchen, including its own flour tortillas.

Art and history museum in Albuquerque, New Mexico

The **Albuquerque Museum**, formerly known as the **Albuquerque Museum of Art and History**, is a public art and history museum in [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico"). It is located in the [Old Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque") area and is operated by the City of Albuquerque Department of Arts & Culture.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-2)

The Albuquerque Museum is dedicated to preserving the art of the American Southwest and the history of Albuquerque and the Middle [Rio Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Grande "Rio Grande") Valley of [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"). The museum also contributes significantly to the cultural and educational programs in the city of Albuquerque. The museum features art of the [Southwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_United_States "Southwestern United States") and its global influences, as well as 400 years of [Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque "Albuquerque") history with permanent installations and special exhibitions of national and international origin.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-AM:_About-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The museum opened as the Museum of Albuquerque in 1967, operating out of a temporary location in the recently vacated [Old Albuquerque Municipal Airport Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Albuquerque_Municipal_Airport_Building "Old Albuquerque Municipal Airport Building").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-3) In 1975, voters approved a [bond issue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_issue "Bond issue") to fund construction of a new, permanent location on the site of a former truck terminal in [Old Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque"). The building was designed by local architect [Antoine Predock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Predock "Antoine Predock") and opened in 1979.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-4) A major expansion designed by Rohde May Keller McNamara Architecture (RMKM) was completed in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-5)

## Exhibits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Exhibits")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Blumenschein-Star_Road_and_White_Sun_1920.jpg/250px-Blumenschein-Star_Road_and_White_Sun_1920.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Blumenschein-Star_Road_and_White_Sun_1920.jpg)

_Star Road and White Sun_ by [Ernest L. Blumenschein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_L._Blumenschein "Ernest L. Blumenschein"), 1920

The museum's permanent exhibits are dedicated to art in New Mexico, and the history of Albuquerque include early maps, [conquistador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador") armor, weavings, and other artifacts of colonial life in New Mexico. The museum also hosts changing exhibits, a massive photo archive, art galleries, and maintains an outdoor [sculpture garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sculpture_garden "Sculpture garden") on the grounds. The museum's collections include 10,000 artworks, 35,000 historical objects, and 130,000 photographs in the photo archive.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-6)

### Permanent exhibits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Permanent exhibits")]

The museum has three permanent exhibits:[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-7)

*   _Common Ground: Art in New Mexico_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-8)
*   _Only in Albuquerque_[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-9)
*   _Sculpture Garden_ (the City of Albuquerque provides a [mobile app](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_app "Mobile app") guide to the Garden)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-10)

### La Jornada

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: La Jornada")]

Located in the sculpture garden is the sculpture [La Jornada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Juan_de_O%C3%B1ate_(Albuquerque,_New_Mexico) "Statue of Juan de Oñate (Albuquerque, New Mexico)"), which was removed from public view in 2020 and later restored to the museum garden.

## Casa San Ysidro

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casa San Ysidro")]

The Albuquerque Museum also operates tours for a late 18th-century house in [Corrales, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrales,_New_Mexico "Corrales, New Mexico"), called **Casa San Ysidro**. The house features a recreation of a 19th-century rancho, including a family chapel, a central plazuela and an enclosed corral area.

The **Albuquerque Museum**, formerly known as the **Albuquerque Museum of Art and History**, is a public art and history museum in [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico"). It is located in the [Old Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque") area and is operated by the City of Albuquerque Department of Arts & Culture.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-2)

The Albuquerque Museum is dedicated to preserving the art of the American Southwest and the history of Albuquerque and the Middle [Rio Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Grande "Rio Grande") Valley of [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"). The museum also contributes significantly to the cultural and educational programs in the city of Albuquerque. The museum features art of the [Southwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwestern_United_States "Southwestern United States") and its global influences, as well as 400 years of [Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque "Albuquerque") history with permanent installations and special exhibitions of national and international origin.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-AM:_About-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The museum opened as the Museum of Albuquerque in 1967, operating out of a temporary location in the recently vacated [Old Albuquerque Municipal Airport Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Albuquerque_Municipal_Airport_Building "Old Albuquerque Municipal Airport Building").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-3) In 1975, voters approved a [bond issue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_issue "Bond issue") to fund construction of a new, permanent location on the site of a former truck terminal in [Old Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque"). The building was designed by local architect [Antoine Predock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Predock "Antoine Predock") and opened in 1979.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-4) A major expansion designed by Rohde May Keller McNamara Architecture (RMKM) was completed in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-5)

## Exhibits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Exhibits")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Blumenschein-Star_Road_and_White_Sun_1920.jpg/250px-Blumenschein-Star_Road_and_White_Sun_1920.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Blumenschein-Star_Road_and_White_Sun_1920.jpg)

_Star Road and White Sun_ by [Ernest L. Blumenschein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_L._Blumenschein "Ernest L. Blumenschein"), 1920

The museum's permanent exhibits are dedicated to art in New Mexico, and the history of Albuquerque include early maps, [conquistador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador") armor, weavings, and other artifacts of colonial life in New Mexico. The museum also hosts changing exhibits, a massive photo archive, art galleries, and maintains an outdoor [sculpture garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sculpture_garden "Sculpture garden") on the grounds. The museum's collections include 10,000 artworks, 35,000 historical objects, and 130,000 photographs in the photo archive.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-6)

### Permanent exhibits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Permanent exhibits")]

The museum has three permanent exhibits:[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-7)

*   _Common Ground: Art in New Mexico_[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-8)
*   _Only in Albuquerque_[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-9)
*   _Sculpture Garden_ (the City of Albuquerque provides a [mobile app](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_app "Mobile app") guide to the Garden)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History#cite_note-10)

### La Jornada

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: La Jornada")]

Located in the sculpture garden is the sculpture [La Jornada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Juan_de_O%C3%B1ate_(Albuquerque,_New_Mexico) "Statue of Juan de Oñate (Albuquerque, New Mexico)"), which was removed from public view in 2020 and later restored to the museum garden.

## Casa San Ysidro

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Albuquerque_Museum_of_Art_and_History&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casa San Ysidro")]

The Albuquerque Museum also operates tours for a late 18th-century house in [Corrales, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrales,_New_Mexico "Corrales, New Mexico"), called **Casa San Ysidro**. The house features a recreation of a 19th-century rancho, including a family chapel, a central plazuela and an enclosed corral area.

Chances are it's somewhere in Santa Fe, _The City Different_, exploring one of America’s most historic, artistic, and fascinating cities.Maybe it's taking a break to eat our famous green chile cheeseburgers. It could be relaxing at one of our world-class spas, discovering Santa Fe's magical healing properties. We boast the world-famous Santa Fe Margarita Trail, too, so there's also the possibility that the page you were looking for is off on a margarita adventure unlike any other. Don't fret though. The **New Mexico Museum of Art** is an art museum in [Santa Fe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico") governed by the state of [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), United States. It is one of four state-run museums in Santa Fe that are part of the [Museum of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_New_Mexico "Museum of New Mexico"). It is located one block off the historic [Santa Fe Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Plaza "Santa Fe Plaza"). It was given its current name in 2007, having previously been referred to as The Museum of Fine Arts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-2)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The building was designed by architect [Isaac Rapp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Rapp "Isaac Rapp") and completed in 1917.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTESheppard198883%E2%80%9388-3) It is an example of [Pueblo Revival Style architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo_Revival_Style_architecture "Pueblo Revival Style architecture"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilson1997[[Category:Wikipedia_articles_needing_page_number_citations_from_November_2021]]%3Csup_class=%22noprint_Inline-Template_%22_style=%22white-space:nowrap;%22%3E[%3Ci%3E[[Wikipedia:Citing_sources|%3Cspan_title=%22This_citation_requires_a_reference_to_the_specific_page_or_range_of_pages_in_which_the_material_appears. (November_2021)%22%3Epage needed%3C/span%3E]]%3C/i%3E]%3C/sup%3E-4) and one of Santa Fe's best-known representations of the synthesis of [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") and [Spanish Colonial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Colonial "Spanish Colonial") design styles. The façade was based on the mission churches of [Acoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoma_Pueblo "Acoma Pueblo"), [San Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Felipe_Pueblo,_New_Mexico "San Felipe Pueblo, New Mexico"), [Cochiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cochiti "Cochiti"), [Laguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laguna_Pueblo "Laguna Pueblo"), [Santa Ana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ana_Pueblo "Santa Ana Pueblo") and [Pecos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pecos_National_Historical_Park "Pecos National Historical Park").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-5)

In September 2023, the museum opened Vladem Contemporary in the Railyard district as a dedicated venue for contemporary art.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-7)

## Collections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Collections")]

The museum’s art collection includes over 20,000 paintings, photographs, sculptures, prints, drawings and mixed-media works. Notable artists in the collection include [Ansel Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansel_Adams "Ansel Adams"), [Gustave Baumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustave_Baumann "Gustave Baumann"), [Brian O'Connor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_O'Connor_(artist) "Brian O'Connor (artist)"), [Georgia O'Keeffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_O'Keeffe "Georgia O'Keeffe"), [Fritz Scholder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fritz_Scholder "Fritz Scholder"), [T. C. Cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._C._Cannon "T. C. Cannon"), [Bruce Nauman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Nauman "Bruce Nauman"), [Luis Jimenez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Jim%C3%A9nez_(sculptor) "Luis Jiménez (sculptor)"), [Maria Martinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Martinez "Maria Martinez"), members of the [Ashcan School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashcan_School "Ashcan School"), [Los Cinco Pintores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Cinco_Pintores "Los Cinco Pintores"), Transcendental Painting Group, and the [Taos Society of Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taos_Society_of_Artists "Taos Society of Artists").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJaques2012186%E2%80%93187-8)

## St. Francis Auditorium

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: St. Francis Auditorium")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/FacilityStF.jpg/250px-FacilityStF.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FacilityStF.jpg)

St. Francis Auditorium

The St. Francis Auditorium, located in the New Mexico Museum of Art, is the venue for various cultural and musical organizations, including the [Santa Fe Chamber Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Chamber_Music_Festival "Santa Fe Chamber Music Festival") and the [Santa Fe Community Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Community_Orchestra?action=edit&redlink=1 "Santa Fe Community Orchestra (page does not exist)"). The auditorium has a seating capacity of 450.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-9) The auditorium displays several murals depicting [St. Francis of Assisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Francis_of_Assisi "St. Francis of Assisi") which were originally designed by Donald Beauregard and completed by [Carlos Vierra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Vierra "Carlos Vierra") and [Kenneth M. Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_M._Chapman "Kenneth M. Chapman").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTESheppard1989[[Category:Wikipedia_articles_needing_page_number_citations_from_November_2021]]%3Csup_class=%22noprint_Inline-Template_%22_style=%22white-space:nowrap;%22%3E[%3Ci%3E[[Wikipedia:Citing_sources|%3Cspan_title=%22This_citation_requires_a_reference_to_the_specific_page_or_range_of_pages_in_which_the_material_appears. ## Vladem Contemporary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Vladem Contemporary")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/VlademPano_230827.jpg/250px-VlademPano_230827.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:VlademPano_230827.jpg)

The New Mexico Museum of Art Vladem Contemporary.

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Vladem_Contemporary_view_from_Garfield.jpg/250px-Vladem_Contemporary_view_from_Garfield.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vladem_Contemporary_view_from_Garfield.jpg)

Vladem Contemporary, view from Garfield.

The Vladem Contemporary Annex of the New Mexico Museum of Art is scheduled to open in September 2023. The annex will house the New Mexico Museum of Art's contemporary collections and shows.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-13) The renovation project is an adaptive reuse of the 1936 Charles Ilfeld Warehouse (repurposed and renamed as the State of New Mexico's Joseph F Halpin Records Building). The annex is named for philanthropists Bob and Ellen Vladem.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-16)

Art museum in New Mexico, U.S.

The **New Mexico Museum of Art** is an art museum in [Santa Fe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico") governed by the state of [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), United States. It is one of four state-run museums in Santa Fe that are part of the [Museum of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_New_Mexico "Museum of New Mexico"). It is located one block off the historic [Santa Fe Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Plaza "Santa Fe Plaza"). It was given its current name in 2007, having previously been referred to as The Museum of Fine Arts.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-2)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The building was designed by architect [Isaac Rapp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Rapp "Isaac Rapp") and completed in 1917.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTESheppard198883%E2%80%9388-3) It is an example of [Pueblo Revival Style architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo_Revival_Style_architecture "Pueblo Revival Style architecture"),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilson1997[[Category:Wikipedia_articles_needing_page_number_citations_from_November_2021]]%3Csup_class=%22noprint_Inline-Template_%22_style=%22white-space:nowrap;%22%3E[%3Ci%3E[[Wikipedia:Citing_sources|%3Cspan_title=%22This_citation_requires_a_reference_to_the_specific_page_or_range_of_pages_in_which_the_material_appears. (November_2021)%22%3Epage needed%3C/span%3E]]%3C/i%3E]%3C/sup%3E-4) and one of Santa Fe's best-known representations of the synthesis of [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") and [Spanish Colonial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Colonial "Spanish Colonial") design styles. The façade was based on the mission churches of [Acoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoma_Pueblo "Acoma Pueblo"), [San Felipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Felipe_Pueblo,_New_Mexico "San Felipe Pueblo, New Mexico"), [Cochiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cochiti "Cochiti"), [Laguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laguna_Pueblo "Laguna Pueblo"), [Santa Ana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ana_Pueblo "Santa Ana Pueblo") and [Pecos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pecos_National_Historical_Park "Pecos National Historical Park").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-5)

In September 2023, the museum opened Vladem Contemporary in the Railyard district as a dedicated venue for contemporary art.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-7)

## Collections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Collections")]

The museum’s art collection includes over 20,000 paintings, photographs, sculptures, prints, drawings and mixed-media works. Notable artists in the collection include [Ansel Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansel_Adams "Ansel Adams"), [Gustave Baumann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustave_Baumann "Gustave Baumann"), [Brian O'Connor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_O'Connor_(artist) "Brian O'Connor (artist)"), [Georgia O'Keeffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_O'Keeffe "Georgia O'Keeffe"), [Fritz Scholder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fritz_Scholder "Fritz Scholder"), [T. C. Cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._C._Cannon "T. C. Cannon"), [Bruce Nauman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Nauman "Bruce Nauman"), [Luis Jimenez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Jim%C3%A9nez_(sculptor) "Luis Jiménez (sculptor)"), [Maria Martinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Martinez "Maria Martinez"), members of the [Ashcan School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashcan_School "Ashcan School"), [Los Cinco Pintores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Cinco_Pintores "Los Cinco Pintores"), Transcendental Painting Group, and the [Taos Society of Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taos_Society_of_Artists "Taos Society of Artists").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJaques2012186%E2%80%93187-8)

## St. Francis Auditorium

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: St. Francis Auditorium")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/FacilityStF.jpg/250px-FacilityStF.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FacilityStF.jpg)

St. Francis Auditorium

The St. Francis Auditorium, located in the New Mexico Museum of Art, is the venue for various cultural and musical organizations, including the [Santa Fe Chamber Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Chamber_Music_Festival "Santa Fe Chamber Music Festival") and the [Santa Fe Community Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Community_Orchestra?action=edit&redlink=1 "Santa Fe Community Orchestra (page does not exist)"). The auditorium has a seating capacity of 450.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-9) The auditorium displays several murals depicting [St. Francis of Assisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Francis_of_Assisi "St. Francis of Assisi") which were originally designed by Donald Beauregard and completed by [Carlos Vierra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Vierra "Carlos Vierra") and [Kenneth M. Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_M._Chapman "Kenneth M. Chapman").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTESheppard1989[[Category:Wikipedia_articles_needing_page_number_citations_from_November_2021]]%3Csup_class=%22noprint_Inline-Template_%22_style=%22white-space:nowrap;%22%3E[%3Ci%3E[[Wikipedia:Citing_sources|%3Cspan_title=%22This_citation_requires_a_reference_to_the_specific_page_or_range_of_pages_in_which_the_material_appears. (November_2021)%22%3Epage needed%3C/span%3E]]%3C/i%3E]%3C/sup%3E-10)

## Library

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Library")]

The museum library contains art books, periodicals, biographical files of artists whose work is collected by the museum and catalogs of the museum's exhibitions since 1917.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFromme198197-11)

## Vladem Contemporary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Vladem Contemporary")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/54/VlademPano_230827.jpg/250px-VlademPano_230827.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:VlademPano_230827.jpg)

The New Mexico Museum of Art Vladem Contemporary.

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Vladem_Contemporary_view_from_Garfield.jpg/250px-Vladem_Contemporary_view_from_Garfield.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vladem_Contemporary_view_from_Garfield.jpg)

Vladem Contemporary, view from Garfield.

The Vladem Contemporary Annex of the New Mexico Museum of Art is scheduled to open in September 2023. The annex will house the New Mexico Museum of Art's contemporary collections and shows.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Art#cite_note-13) The renovation project is an adaptive reuse of the 1936 Charles Ilfeld Warehouse (repurposed and renamed as the State of New Mexico's Joseph F Halpin Records Building). # La Choza

The local’s choice for chile!

Located in the old adobe headquarters of turn of the century Mercer Ranch, La Choza’s warm, friendly atmosphere, authentic dishes, great margaritas, and colorful decor welcomes those needing to get their chile fix. La Choza is truly Santa Fe dining that reflects the heritage of past & present and is the sister restaurant to another locals’ favorite, **[The Shed](http://www.sfshed.com/)**.

The **Institute of American Indian Arts** (**IAIA**) is a [public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_college "Public college")[tribal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribal_colleges_and_universities "Tribal colleges and universities")[land-grant college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land-grant_university "Land-grant university") in [Santa Fe, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico"), United States. The college focuses on [Native American art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_art "Native American art"). It operates the Museum of Contemporary [Native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") Arts (MoCNA), which is housed in the historic Santa Fe [Federal Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Building "Federal Building") (the old Post Office), a landmark [Pueblo Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo_Revival "Pueblo Revival") building listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") as **Federal Building**. The museum houses the National Collection of Contemporary Indian Art, with more than 7,000 items.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Institute_of_American_Indian_Arts&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The Institute of American Indian Arts was co-founded by [Lloyd Kiva New](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Kiva_New "Lloyd Kiva New") ([Cherokee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherokee "Cherokee"), 1916–2002) and Dr. George Boyce in 1962 with funding from the [Bureau of Indian Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Indian_Affairs "Bureau of Indian Affairs").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-nyt-3) The school was founded upon the recommendation of the BIA Department of Education and the [Indian Arts and Crafts Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Arts_and_Crafts_Board "Indian Arts and Crafts Board"). Three factors led to the school's founding: growing dissatisfaction with the academic program at the [Santa Fe Indian School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Indian_School "Santa Fe Indian School"), the BIA's emerging interest in higher education, and the influence of the Southwest Indian Art Project and the [Rockefeller Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Foundation "Rockefeller Foundation").

IAIA began on the SFIS campus in October 1962. From 1962 to 1979, IAIA ran a high school program, and began offering college- and [graduate-level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduate-level "Graduate-level") art courses in 1975. In 1986, the Institute of American Indian and Alaska Native Culture and Arts Development was [congressionally chartered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_charter "Congressional charter") as a [nonprofit organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization"), similar to the structure of the [Smithsonian Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_Institution "Smithsonian Institution"), which separated the school from the BIA. It was designated a [land-grant college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land-grant_university "Land-grant university") in 1994 alongside 31 other tribal colleges.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-4) In 2001, the school was [accredited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accreditation "Accreditation"), including the accreditation of [four year degrees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_year_degree "Four year degree"). A two-year [low-residency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-residency_program "Low-residency program")[MFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Fine_Arts "Master of Fine Arts") in creative writing was accredited in 2013.

Today, IAIA sits on a 140-acre (57 ha) campus 12 miles (19 km) south of downtown Santa Fe and also operates the Museum of Contemporary Native Art, which is located in [Santa Fe Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Plaza "Santa Fe Plaza"), as well as the Center for Lifelong Education.

## Partnerships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Institute_of_American_Indian_Arts&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Partnerships")]

IAIA is a member of the [American Indian Higher Education Consortium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Indian_Higher_Education_Consortium "American Indian Higher Education Consortium"), which includes tribally and federally chartered institutions working to strengthen [tribal nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribal_nation "Tribal nation") and make a difference in the lives of [American Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") and [Alaska Natives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska_Natives "Alaska Natives"). IAIA generally serves geographically isolated populations of Native Americans that have few other means of accessing education beyond the high school level.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-aihec.org-6)

During the early 1970s, faculty member Ed Wapp, Jr.'s E-Yah-Pah-Hah Chanters toured nationally with the [Hanay Geiogamah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanay_Geiogamah "Hanay Geiogamah")'s American Indian Theatre Ensemble, a [company in residence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist-in-residence "Artist-in-residence") at [La MaMa Experimental Theatre Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_MaMa_Experimental_Theatre_Club "La MaMa Experimental Theatre Club") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-7) A program from this tour describes the musical ensemble as "students from the Institute of American Indian Arts at Santa Fe, N.M., and are under the direction of Ed Wapp, Jr. Their music is presented in both the traditional and contemporary American Indian forms. Songs are selected from the Plains, Eastern, Great Basin, Southwest and Northwest Coast areas of Indian Country."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-8)

The **Institute of American Indian Arts** (**IAIA**) is a [public](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_college "Public college")[tribal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribal_colleges_and_universities "Tribal colleges and universities")[land-grant college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land-grant_university "Land-grant university") in [Santa Fe, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe,_New_Mexico "Santa Fe, New Mexico"), United States. The college focuses on [Native American art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_art "Native American art"). It operates the Museum of Contemporary [Native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") Arts (MoCNA), which is housed in the historic Santa Fe [Federal Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Building "Federal Building") (the old Post Office), a landmark [Pueblo Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo_Revival "Pueblo Revival") building listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") as **Federal Building**. The museum houses the National Collection of Contemporary Indian Art, with more than 7,000 items.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Institute_of_American_Indian_Arts&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The Institute of American Indian Arts was co-founded by [Lloyd Kiva New](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Kiva_New "Lloyd Kiva New") ([Cherokee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherokee "Cherokee"), 1916–2002) and Dr. George Boyce in 1962 with funding from the [Bureau of Indian Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Indian_Affairs "Bureau of Indian Affairs").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-nyt-3) The school was founded upon the recommendation of the BIA Department of Education and the [Indian Arts and Crafts Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Arts_and_Crafts_Board "Indian Arts and Crafts Board"). Three factors led to the school's founding: growing dissatisfaction with the academic program at the [Santa Fe Indian School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Indian_School "Santa Fe Indian School"), the BIA's emerging interest in higher education, and the influence of the Southwest Indian Art Project and the [Rockefeller Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockefeller_Foundation "Rockefeller Foundation").

IAIA began on the SFIS campus in October 1962. From 1962 to 1979, IAIA ran a high school program, and began offering college- and [graduate-level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graduate-level "Graduate-level") art courses in 1975. In 1986, the Institute of American Indian and Alaska Native Culture and Arts Development was [congressionally chartered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_charter "Congressional charter") as a [nonprofit organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization"), similar to the structure of the [Smithsonian Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smithsonian_Institution "Smithsonian Institution"), which separated the school from the BIA. It was designated a [land-grant college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land-grant_university "Land-grant university") in 1994 alongside 31 other tribal colleges.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-4) In 2001, the school was [accredited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accreditation "Accreditation"), including the accreditation of [four year degrees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_year_degree "Four year degree"). A two-year [low-residency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low-residency_program "Low-residency program")[MFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Fine_Arts "Master of Fine Arts") in creative writing was accredited in 2013.

Today, IAIA sits on a 140-acre (57 ha) campus 12 miles (19 km) south of downtown Santa Fe and also operates the Museum of Contemporary Native Art, which is located in [Santa Fe Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Plaza "Santa Fe Plaza"), as well as the Center for Lifelong Education.

## IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Institute_of_American_Indian_Arts&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts")]

Main article: [IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAIA_Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts "IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts")
