In 1991 the college founded the Institute of American Indian Arts Museum, now the IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts (MoCNA), in downtown Santa Fe, with a focus on contemporary intertribal [Native American art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_art "Native American art"), the MoCNA is housed in the historic Santa Fe Federal Building (the old Post Office), a landmark [Pueblo Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pueblo_Revival "Pueblo Revival") building listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-5) The museum also features the [Allan Houser Sculpture Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allan_Houser "Allan Houser").

## Partnerships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Institute_of_American_Indian_Arts&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Partnerships")]

IAIA is a member of the [American Indian Higher Education Consortium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Indian_Higher_Education_Consortium "American Indian Higher Education Consortium"), which includes tribally and federally chartered institutions working to strengthen [tribal nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribal_nation "Tribal nation") and make a difference in the lives of [American Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") and [Alaska Natives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska_Natives "Alaska Natives"). IAIA generally serves geographically isolated populations of Native Americans that have few other means of accessing education beyond the high school level.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-aihec.org-6)

During the early 1970s, faculty member Ed Wapp, Jr.'s E-Yah-Pah-Hah Chanters toured nationally with the [Hanay Geiogamah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanay_Geiogamah "Hanay Geiogamah")'s American Indian Theatre Ensemble, a [company in residence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist-in-residence "Artist-in-residence") at [La MaMa Experimental Theatre Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_MaMa_Experimental_Theatre_Club "La MaMa Experimental Theatre Club") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-7) A program from this tour describes the musical ensemble as "students from the Institute of American Indian Arts at Santa Fe, N.M., and are under the direction of Ed Wapp, Jr. Their music is presented in both the traditional and contemporary American Indian forms. Songs are selected from the Plains, Eastern, Great Basin, Southwest and Northwest Coast areas of Indian Country."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Contemporary_Native_Arts#cite_note-8)

The **New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science** is a [natural history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_history "Natural history") and [science museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_museum "Science museum") in [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico") near [Old Town Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque"). The Museum was founded in 1986.[[1]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-1) It operates as a public revenue facility of the New Mexico Department of Cultural Affairs.

## History

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The museum was created by an act of the [New Mexico Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Legislature "New Mexico Legislature") signed into law by Governor [Bruce King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_King "Bruce King") in March 1980.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-2) Part of the motivation for the project was to provide a home for some of the numerous dinosaur fossils discovered in New Mexico rather than sending them to out-of-state institutions.[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-3) Ground was broken on a 4.8-acre (1.9 ha) site near [Old Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque") and the museum opened on January 11, 1986. It was one of the first new natural history museums in the U.S. in decades and represented an updated approach focusing on interactive multimedia exhibits rather than large collections of specimens displayed in glass cases.[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-4) An astronomy center including an observatory and planetarium was added to the museum in 1999. This was originally a separate museum operated by the [University of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_New_Mexico "University of New Mexico"), but was merged into the Museum of Natural History and Science in 2007.[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-5)[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-6)

## Permanent exhibits

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Permanent exhibits")]

Time Tracks, the Museum's permanent exhibit halls illustrate a journey through time, covering the birth of the Universe (≈13.6 billion years ago) to the [Ice Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleistocene "Pleistocene") (≈10,000 years ago). The eight journey through time halls are as follows:

*   Bradbury Stamm Construction Hall of Ancient Life
*   Dawn of the Dinosaurs
*   Jurassic Age of Super Giants
*   New Mexico's Seacoast
*   Age of Volcanoes
*   Rise of the Recent - Evolving Grasslands
*   Cave Experience
*   New Mexico's Ice Age

Other permanent exhibits include an interactive [planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium "Planetarium") where programs are held daily.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) There is also a floor of exhibit galleries dedicated to astronomy and space exploration, as well as an observation deck for viewing through the telescope. The observatory opens only occasionally, usually during evenings when the museum itself is open to the public. The Fossilworks exhibit shows people removing material from fossilized dinosaur bones.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) The museum houses a "Naturalist Center" that is home to live animals and insects, and there is also a geologic exhibit on the minerals of the region.

## Temporary exhibits

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Temporary exhibits")]

**Current Exhibits**_Back to Bones_ features "everything from 300-million-year-old fish and early reptiles, dinosaur skulls from near the end of the Age of Reptiles, to Ice Age mammals," according to Paleontology Curator Thomas A. Williamson. The exhibit was originally conceived to showcase New Mexican fossils not only to the public, but also to visiting members of the [Society of Vertebrate Paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Vertebrate_Paleontology "Society of Vertebrate Paleontology") during Albuquerque's hosting of the SVP meeting in October 2018.[[8]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-8) The exhibit was renewed in October 2019 and was still on display as of January 2021.

**Previous Exhibits** Until early 2017, the New Mexico Museum of Natural History was home to _STARTUP: Albuquerque and the Personal Computer Revolution_. This exhibit was dedicated to the history of the [personal computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computer "Personal computer") and operated for ten years, being based on a concept by Microsoft co-founder [Paul G. Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen "Paul Allen"), who along with [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates") started [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") in Albuquerque. In May 2007, two exhibits in the _STARTUP_ Gallery won MUSE awards from the [American Alliance of Museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Alliance_of_Museums "American Alliance of Museums"): _Pizza Run - A Slice of Programming_ won a Silver Level MUSE Award in the category of Interactive Kiosks, and the artifact theater _Rise of the Machines_ won a Gold Level MUSE Award in the Multimedia Installations Category. In 2017, the museum relinquished control of this exhibit to Paul Allen to use at his Living Computer Museum + Labs in Seattle, WA.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-9)

The museum previously hosted an exhibit entitled _Wild Music_ from June 2017 through January 2018. The exhibit showcased an interactive collection of both natural and artificial musical displays on the second floor, all with fully bilingual signage. Acoustical physics and musical theory are presented in various ways and from various parts of the world.[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-10)

In February 2018 through August of the same year, the museum brought in _Da Vinci: The Genius_ to display recreations of the art and scientific inventions of Leonardo da Vinci. Produced by Grande Exhibitions, the replicas of da Vinci's art and machines focused on the extraordinary achievements of one of the renaissance's most famous and influential people.[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-11) Composed of two distinct sections, _Da Vinci: The Genius_ firstly looked deeply into his art, taking a forensic approach to dissecting the Mona Lisa with "The Secrets of Mona Lisa". Secondly, "The Inventions" portion showed 75 separate devices, both small scale and life-sized, invented by Leonardo da Vinci.[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-12)

_Picturing the Past_ was a juried exhibition of paleo-art. The gallery featured art from artists worldwide, focusing on prehistoric creatures. The work of local paleoartist [Matt Celeskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Celeskey?action=edit&redlink=1 "Matt Celeskey (page does not exist)") featured heavily. This exhibit was on display through January 2019.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-13)

_Drugs: Costs and Consequences_ was an exhibit that discussed illicit drugs. The exhibit was on display until December 8, 2019.[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-14)

_Brain: The Inside Story_ was a traveling exhibition on loan from the American Museum of Natural History. It used hands-on displays to explore senses, emotions, and brain development. Using current research and technology, the exhibit focused on the latest in neuroscience to highlight the brain's amazing abilities in function and adaptation. This exhibit was at the museum until November 10, 2019, after which it was permanently retired, and did not go on to be displayed elsewhere.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-15)

**Upcoming Exhibits** No upcoming exhibits are currently available.

### Dinosaurs exhibited

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Dinosaurs exhibited")]

The _Jurassic Super Giants_ exhibit features the complete skeletons of _[Seismosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seismosaurus "Seismosaurus")_, _[Saurophaganax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saurophaganax "Saurophaganax")_, _[Stegosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stegosaurus "Stegosaurus")_, and one leg of a _[Brachiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachiosaurus "Brachiosaurus")_. Previously, in the museum's atrium was the skeleton of [Stan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Specimens_of_Tyrannosaurus#%22Stan%22:_BHI_3033 "Specimens of Tyrannosaurus"), a _[Tyrannosaurus rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus "Tyrannosaurus")_ measuring forty feet (≈12.2 meters) in length and twelve feet (≈3.7 meters) in height, the second largest _T. rex_ ever found. Stan currently resides at the Farmington Museum in Farmington, NM. Stan was replaced in the atrium during the summer of 2019 by an animatronic Bisti Beast, or _[Bistahieversor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistahieversor "Bistahieversor")_, dinosaur.[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-16)

Bronze statues of two dinosaurs created by artist David A. Thomas, a _[Pentaceratops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentaceratops "Pentaceratops")_ named "Spike" and an _[Albertosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertosaurus "Albertosaurus")_ named "Alberta", stand at the entrance.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) Spike and Alberta were installed at the museum in the mid-1980s, with Spike being put in place in 1985[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-17) and Alberta joining a few years later in 1987.[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-18) Many dinosaur [fossils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossils "Fossils") have been found in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), and a few of the ones on display in the museum are only known from New Mexico.

## Other features

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other features")]

The Museum also houses changing exhibits, NatureWorks Discovery Store, as well as the Dynatheater, which is a 3-D [theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movie_theater "Movie theater") similar to [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX"). The films shown are typically documentary style, focusing on a broad range of subjects. The exterior of the museum features "A Walk Through New Mexico," a landscape representation of the topographical and geologic features of New Mexico.

The **New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science** is a [natural history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_history "Natural history") and [science museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_museum "Science museum") in [Albuquerque, New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico "Albuquerque, New Mexico") near [Old Town Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque"). The Museum was founded in 1986.[[1]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-1) It operates as a public revenue facility of the New Mexico Department of Cultural Affairs.

## History

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The museum was created by an act of the [New Mexico Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Legislature "New Mexico Legislature") signed into law by Governor [Bruce King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_King "Bruce King") in March 1980.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-2) Part of the motivation for the project was to provide a home for some of the numerous dinosaur fossils discovered in New Mexico rather than sending them to out-of-state institutions.[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-3) Ground was broken on a 4.8-acre (1.9 ha) site near [Old Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Town_Albuquerque "Old Town Albuquerque") and the museum opened on January 11, 1986. It was one of the first new natural history museums in the U.S. in decades and represented an updated approach focusing on interactive multimedia exhibits rather than large collections of specimens displayed in glass cases.[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-4) An astronomy center including an observatory and planetarium was added to the museum in 1999. This was originally a separate museum operated by the [University of New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_New_Mexico "University of New Mexico"), but was merged into the Museum of Natural History and Science in 2007.[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-5)[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-6)

## Permanent exhibits

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Permanent exhibits")]

Time Tracks, the Museum's permanent exhibit halls illustrate a journey through time, covering the birth of the Universe (≈13.6 billion years ago) to the [Ice Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleistocene "Pleistocene") (≈10,000 years ago). The eight journey through time halls are as follows:

*   Bradbury Stamm Construction Hall of Ancient Life
*   Dawn of the Dinosaurs
*   Jurassic Age of Super Giants
*   New Mexico's Seacoast
*   Age of Volcanoes
*   Rise of the Recent - Evolving Grasslands
*   Cave Experience
*   New Mexico's Ice Age

Other permanent exhibits include an interactive [planetarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planetarium "Planetarium") where programs are held daily.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) There is also a floor of exhibit galleries dedicated to astronomy and space exploration, as well as an observation deck for viewing through the telescope. The observatory opens only occasionally, usually during evenings when the museum itself is open to the public. The Fossilworks exhibit shows people removing material from fossilized dinosaur bones.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) The museum houses a "Naturalist Center" that is home to live animals and insects, and there is also a geologic exhibit on the minerals of the region.

## Temporary exhibits

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Temporary exhibits")]

**Current Exhibits**_Back to Bones_ features "everything from 300-million-year-old fish and early reptiles, dinosaur skulls from near the end of the Age of Reptiles, to Ice Age mammals," according to Paleontology Curator Thomas A. Williamson. The exhibit was originally conceived to showcase New Mexican fossils not only to the public, but also to visiting members of the [Society of Vertebrate Paleontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_of_Vertebrate_Paleontology "Society of Vertebrate Paleontology") during Albuquerque's hosting of the SVP meeting in October 2018.[[8]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-8) The exhibit was renewed in October 2019 and was still on display as of January 2021.

**Previous Exhibits** Until early 2017, the New Mexico Museum of Natural History was home to _STARTUP: Albuquerque and the Personal Computer Revolution_. This exhibit was dedicated to the history of the [personal computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_computer "Personal computer") and operated for ten years, being based on a concept by Microsoft co-founder [Paul G. Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen "Paul Allen"), who along with [Bill Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates") started [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") in Albuquerque. In May 2007, two exhibits in the _STARTUP_ Gallery won MUSE awards from the [American Alliance of Museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Alliance_of_Museums "American Alliance of Museums"): _Pizza Run - A Slice of Programming_ won a Silver Level MUSE Award in the category of Interactive Kiosks, and the artifact theater _Rise of the Machines_ won a Gold Level MUSE Award in the Multimedia Installations Category. In 2017, the museum relinquished control of this exhibit to Paul Allen to use at his Living Computer Museum + Labs in Seattle, WA.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-9)

The museum previously hosted an exhibit entitled _Wild Music_ from June 2017 through January 2018. The exhibit showcased an interactive collection of both natural and artificial musical displays on the second floor, all with fully bilingual signage. Acoustical physics and musical theory are presented in various ways and from various parts of the world.[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-10)

In February 2018 through August of the same year, the museum brought in _Da Vinci: The Genius_ to display recreations of the art and scientific inventions of Leonardo da Vinci. Produced by Grande Exhibitions, the replicas of da Vinci's art and machines focused on the extraordinary achievements of one of the renaissance's most famous and influential people.[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-11) Composed of two distinct sections, _Da Vinci: The Genius_ firstly looked deeply into his art, taking a forensic approach to dissecting the Mona Lisa with "The Secrets of Mona Lisa". Secondly, "The Inventions" portion showed 75 separate devices, both small scale and life-sized, invented by Leonardo da Vinci.[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-12)

_Picturing the Past_ was a juried exhibition of paleo-art. The gallery featured art from artists worldwide, focusing on prehistoric creatures. The work of local paleoartist [Matt Celeskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Celeskey?action=edit&redlink=1 "Matt Celeskey (page does not exist)") featured heavily. This exhibit was on display through January 2019.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-13)

_Drugs: Costs and Consequences_ was an exhibit that discussed illicit drugs. The exhibit was on display until December 8, 2019.[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-14)

_Brain: The Inside Story_ was a traveling exhibition on loan from the American Museum of Natural History. It used hands-on displays to explore senses, emotions, and brain development. Using current research and technology, the exhibit focused on the latest in neuroscience to highlight the brain's amazing abilities in function and adaptation. This exhibit was at the museum until November 10, 2019, after which it was permanently retired, and did not go on to be displayed elsewhere.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-15)

**Upcoming Exhibits** No upcoming exhibits are currently available.

### Dinosaurs exhibited

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Dinosaurs exhibited")]

The _Jurassic Super Giants_ exhibit features the complete skeletons of _[Seismosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seismosaurus "Seismosaurus")_, _[Saurophaganax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saurophaganax "Saurophaganax")_, _[Stegosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stegosaurus "Stegosaurus")_, and one leg of a _[Brachiosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brachiosaurus "Brachiosaurus")_. Previously, in the museum's atrium was the skeleton of [Stan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Specimens_of_Tyrannosaurus#%22Stan%22:_BHI_3033 "Specimens of Tyrannosaurus"), a _[Tyrannosaurus rex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrannosaurus "Tyrannosaurus")_ measuring forty feet (≈12.2 meters) in length and twelve feet (≈3.7 meters) in height, the second largest _T. rex_ ever found. Stan currently resides at the Farmington Museum in Farmington, NM. Stan was replaced in the atrium during the summer of 2019 by an animatronic Bisti Beast, or _[Bistahieversor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistahieversor "Bistahieversor")_, dinosaur.[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-16)

Bronze statues of two dinosaurs created by artist David A. Thomas, a _[Pentaceratops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentaceratops "Pentaceratops")_ named "Spike" and an _[Albertosaurus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albertosaurus "Albertosaurus")_ named "Alberta", stand at the entrance.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-Gerbic2018-7) Spike and Alberta were installed at the museum in the mid-1980s, with Spike being put in place in 1985[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-17) and Alberta joining a few years later in 1987.[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science#cite_note-18) Many dinosaur [fossils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossils "Fossils") have been found in [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), and a few of the ones on display in the museum are only known from New Mexico.

## Other features

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=New_Mexico_Museum_of_Natural_History_and_Science&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other features")]

The Museum also houses changing exhibits, NatureWorks Discovery Store, as well as the Dynatheater, which is a 3-D [theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movie_theater "Movie theater") similar to [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX"). The films shown are typically documentary style, focusing on a broad range of subjects. The exterior of the museum features "A Walk Through New Mexico," a landscape representation of the topographical and geologic features of New Mexico.
